text: My grandfather used to say the redwoods remember everything. So we don't have to.
The summer I turned ten, he took me to see the oldest one.
That morning, he called me by my grandmother's name. I didn't correct him.
Two thousand years ago, this giant was a seed no bigger than a grain of sand.
Fire burned a door right into her heart, and she just kept growing.
That's where he asked my grandmother to marry him.
He carved it there, so the tree would remember for him.
I was gone five minutes. Maybe ten.
I kept hearing his stories in my head.
The night lightning split her crown, and she kept standing.
The fire that burned for a whole summer.
The storm that took the giant beside her.
Then my light went out.
And I remembered. When the fire came, the animals hid inside the tree. And they lived.
For one moment, he knew exactly who I was.
He forgot the tree long before we lost him. But the tree never forgot him.
Now I bring my son here, and I tell him her stories.
Grandpa was starting to forget things. Little things, at first.
When I came back, he was gone.
Five hundred years ago, lightning split her crown, and she kept standing.
Centuries ago, a fire burned through this forest for a whole summer.
A storm knocked down the giant beside her. But not her.
He forgot the tree long before we lost him. But his heart is still there, carved in her bark.
